clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 1 designates the Director of the agency (the International Communication Agency, renamed the United States Information Agency by EO 12388) to determine that imported objects are of cultural significance and that their temporary display is in the national interest, and to publish notices. The 2026-10-02 Department of State notice makes exactly those two determinations and orders their publication, citing this order as authority, so the command is still being applied; the actor is now the Department of State (the notice recites the Foreign Affairs Reform and Restructuring Act of 1998 and State Department delegations), which the held sources show as a substitution of officer, not an end. Before and after EO 12388: the agency name only.

clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 2 requires the Director to consult the Secretary of State on national interest and permits consultation with the Smithsonian, the National Gallery of Art and others on cultural significance. It is a procedural condition on the section 1 determinations, which are still being made (2026-10-02 notice), and no held source ends it; EO 12388 changed only the agency name.

clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 3 authorizes the Director to delegate the functions within the agency; the 2026 notice recites State Department delegations of authority, consistent with continuing delegation, and no held source revokes it; EO 12388 changed only the agency name.

Section 4 reads 'Sec. 4. Executive Order No. 11312 of October 14, 1966 is revoked.' and section 6 reads 'Sec. 6. This Order shall be effective on April 1, 1978.' The revocation therefore took effect on 1978-04-01, when the order took effect, and was performed then; no later date or condition appears and no held source shows a revival of EO 11312.

clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14 as a standing continuation rule. Section 5 keeps in effect any order, regulation, determination or other action that was in effect under EO 11312 until it is changed under this order's authority; no held source shows that every such action has been changed or that the rule was withdrawn, so I record it as operative without claiming that any particular action survives. The earlier EO 11312 text is not held, which is why the claim does not identify the surviving actions.

Section 6 states the order's effective date, 'Sec. 6. This Order shall be effective on April 1, 1978.' It is exhausted by performance when that date arrived (1978-04-01), after which the order's other sections operate; it is not a continuing command.

research_rationale:
EO 12047 (signed 1978-03-27, Jimmy Carter; 43 FR 13359, filed 1978-03-28, printed 1978-03-29) designates the director of the foreign-information agency to exercise the President's functions under the Act of October 19, 1965 (79 Stat. 985, 22 U.S.C. 2459) on imported objects of cultural significance. I read the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12047.txt in full: the preamble and sections 1 through 6 are all present, the six prepared inventory clauses cover every operative section, and identity (number, title, date, signer, page) matches the register row. Later instruments: EO 12388 (signed 1982-10-14, 47 FR 46245; effective as of August 24, 1982 under its section 6) amends sections 1, 2 and 3 only by substituting the agency name; it is the only later order in the held Federal Register disposition notes and the number search of held texts (the other citing texts are the 1989 codification snapshot and a 2026 Department of State notice). The 2026-10-02 notice (91 FR 62802) is current-use evidence that determinations under section 1 are still made in reliance on this order. The U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected) found a note under 22 U.S.C. 2459 printing the order, and the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) was read for coverage; neither records a revocation. Sections 4 and 6 are terminated by performance on 1978-04-01; sections 1, 2, 3 and 5 are operative.
